hasPart.description: Night sweats are when you sweat so much that your night clothes and bedding get soaking wet.

hasPart.text:
It's normal to sweat during the night if the room or your bedding is making you too hot.

Night sweats are when you sweat so much that your night clothes and bedding are soaking wet, even though where you're sleeping is cool.

Adults and children can get night sweats.

hasPart.headline: What night sweats are
See a GP if:
hasPart.text:
• you have night sweats regularly that wake you up or worry you
  • you also have a very high temperature (or feel hot, cold or shivery), a cough or diarrhoea
  • you have night sweats and you're losing weight for no reason

hasPart.description: Treatment is not usually needed for night sweats. But if medicine you’re taking may be causing night sweats, your GP may prescribe a different one.

hasPart.text:
If you have night sweats, you will not usually need treatment, but the GP will want to check if you have any other symptoms.

If you're taking medicine and the GP thinks it might be causing night sweats, they may prescribe a different one.

hasPart.headline: Treatment for night sweats from a GP

hasPart.description: Common causes of night sweats include the menopause, anxiety, medicines, low blood sugar, alcohol or drug use, and excessive sweating (hyperhidrosis).

hasPart.text:
The most common reasons for night sweats are:

  • menopause symptoms ("hot flushes")
  • anxiety
  • medicines, such as some antidepressants, steroids and painkillers
  • low blood sugar (hypoglycaemia)
  • alcohol or drug use
  • a harmless condition called hyperhidrosis that makes you sweat too much all the time

Sometimes the cause of night sweats is unknown.
